prediction:
THOUGHT: The patient is a young postpartum woman with three months of radial styloid/ radial-sided thumb and wrist pain worsened by grasping/holding her infant — a classic overuse pattern. Exam shows localized swelling and tenderness over the radial styloid and a positive Finkelstein’s test, which is highly suggestive of stenosing tenosynovitis of the first dorsal compartment (abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis). The history of a remote fall is less consistent with ongoing scaphoid fracture (would have presented earlier) and there are no systemic signs to suggest inflammatory arthritis; CMC osteoarthritis is less likely given her age and normal finger ROM and absence of a positive grind test. Intersection syndrome typically causes more dorsal forearm pain and crepitus, which are not present. Overall the findings most strongly support de Quervain tenosynovitis. 

DIAGNOSIS: De Quervain tenosynovitis (stenosing tenosynovitis of the first dorsal compartment).
